description: The Canadian Internet Use Survey (CIUS), run by Statistics Canada, measures how Canadians use the internet and digital technologies: where and how often they go online, devices and smartphone use, online government services, social networking, digital skills, e-commerce, online work, and security, privacy and trust, with new questions in 2022 on harmful content, digital credentials, cryptocurrencies, artificial intelligence and gig work. The 2022 cycle was collected by electronic questionnaire and interview from 29 November 2022 to 5 April 2023. Public use microdata files for the 2005, 2007, 2009, 2010, 2012, 2018, 2020 and 2022 cycles, in English and French, are on Borealis through the Data Liberation Initiative, as are forerunners: the Household Internet Use Survey (1997 onwards, for Industry Canada), the Residential Telephone Service Survey (a Labour Force Survey supplement on phone penetration and affordability, 1998) and the National Electronic Media Use Survey (1996). Coverage: Canada by province, with urban and rural detail. Format and access: microdata with codebooks for Data Liberation Initiative member institutions; summary tables are free of charge on the Statistics Canada website under the Statistics Canada Open Licence. Caveats: self-reported use, not service quality; questions change between cycles. Simulation uses: dependence of people and groups on internet and phone services, for social vulnerability weighting of telecom outages. Related records: the NTIA Internet Use Survey and Eurobarometer e-Communications surveys are counterparts.
